abstract: Two cases of primary choriocarcinoma arose in the urinary bladder in males aged 72 and 70 years. Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in serum and urine was significantly elevated in both cases. Cytologic features consisted of bizarre mononucleate and multinucleate giant cells with numerous erythrocytes, necrotic cells and neutrophils, indicating the possibility of choriocarcinoma. Histologically, one tumor consisted of an admixture of choriocarcinomatous areas and transitional cell carcinoma (TCC) with or without syncytiotrophoblastic differentiation, and the other was composed of pure choriocarcinoma. Immunohistochemical examination revealed that syncytiotrophoblasts and a small number of TCC cells were intensely positive for hCG in their cytoplasm. The histogenesis of choriocarcinoma arising in the bladder is considered to be metaplasia or retro-differentiation from TCC to trophoblasts because of TCC's differentiating to hCG-positive trophoblasts, as seen in one of the present cases.
abstract_ja: 2例の膀胱原発絨毛癌が、72歳と70歳の男性で発生した。両例とも血清および尿中のヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)が有意に上昇していた。細胞学的所見では、多数の赤血球、壊死細胞、好中球を伴う奇怪な単核および多核巨細胞がみられ、絨毛癌の可能性が示唆された。組織学的には、一方の腫瘍は絨毛癌成分と移行上皮癌(TCC)（合胞体栄養膜細胞分化の有無を問わず）の混在からなり、他方は純粋な絨毛癌からなっていた。免疫組織化学的検討では、合胞体栄養膜細胞と少数のTCC細胞の細胞質が強くhCG陽性を示した。TCCがhCG陽性の栄養膜細胞へ分化することから、膀胱に発生する絨毛癌の組織発生は、TCCからの化生あるいは逆分化と考えられる。
